title: Treesa-Gayatri Stun Chinese Seeds, End India's 15-Year Wait for Worlds Medal
indian_angle: This historic win secured India's first women's doubles medal at the World Championships in 15 years, a significant achievement for Indian badminton.
summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand delivered a thrilling 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 quarter-final victory over China's Jia and Zhang, guaranteeing India a medal at the BWF World Championships for the first time in women's doubles in 15 years.

title: Satwik-Chirag Exit Worlds in Quarters After Loss to Chinese Pair
indian_angle: India's top men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, were eliminated from the World Championships, ending their medal hopes.
summary: India's star men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, were defeated by China's Chang and Liang in the BWF World Championships quarter-finals with scores of 21-18, 21-9, reportedly amid fitness concerns.

title: Sindhu Exits Worlds After Epic, Doubles Pairs Advance to Quarters
indian_angle: This report covers the end of India's singles campaign with PV Sindhu's valiant fight, while highlighting the continued success of Indian doubles pairs, Satwik-Chirag and Treesa-Gayatri, who advanced to the quarter-finals.
summary: India's singles challenge at the BWF World Championships concluded with PV Sindhu's 88-minute battle ending in defeat, but the country's medal hopes remained alive as both the men's doubles pair of Satwik-Chirag and women's doubles pair of Treesa-Gayatri secured their spots in the quarter-finals.

title: Lakshya Sen Suffers Shock Exit at World Championships
indian_angle: Indian men's singles hopeful Lakshya Sen's unexpected defeat marks a significant development for India's performance at the World Championships.
summary: India's Lakshya Sen was eliminated from the BWF World Championships after a challenging match against American teenager Garret Tan, marking a surprising early exit for the Indian shuttler.

title: Junior National Coaching Camp for Asia U17 & U15 Championships in Guwahati
indian_angle: This news highlights the Badminton Association of India's commitment to nurturing young talent through a national coaching camp for upcoming Asian junior championships, held in Guwahati.
summary: A national coaching camp for the Indian junior badminton team is underway at the National Center of Excellence in Guwahati, preparing players for the Badminton Asia U17 & U15 Junior Championships 2026.

title: BAI's Improved Hosting for World Badminton Championships
indian_angle: This feature details how the Badminton Association of India (BAI) successfully hosted the BWF World Championships after 17 years, implementing significant improvements in facilities based on feedback from the India Open.
summary: The Badminton Association of India (BAI) has successfully hosted the BWF World Championships in India after a 17-year gap, implementing significant improvements in facilities and organization based on lessons learned from the India Open.
